entries.text: Confirm the new Vitest AC tests fail for the right reason before implementing (5 were red here), and do not treat an e2e guard that counts occurrences as the red signal because it passes at baseline.
Seed test fixtures through the write path production uses and test the production read path, because a column production never writes (plans.plan_json here) lets green tests cover only dead data.

entries.text: When an item adds an IPC command, list src/app/shell.test.tsx (the F-30.4 allowed-command list) in the tests stage, because F-04.3 had to add sessionState and sessionResume there outside its planned test files.

A command that only reads caches (restore, resume) should not call the Claude binary lookup (executable()) or any other discovery, because the review found session_resume failing silently without Claude Code although it runs no claude process.

When the PROGRESS line lists commit SHAs for an item, check them first: if the criterion code is already on base, the test stage should add locked tests only and skip the implementer (F-05.5: implementer skipped, reviewer merged with no findings, gate passed on the first run).

For core parsers of git output, build fixtures from real git diffs and run the production to_model path with spaces, Polish characters and CRLF or missing-final-newline cases, because the review accepted this as non-tautological and independent of autocrlf (F-05.5, 6 integration tests, no findings).

When a core flag reaches a screen (Hunk.mechanical feeding the Skim row), set it in the mock backend in the same item, and first list the existing tests that read the unflagged rows so they stay green with the flag set, because F-05.5 left it unset so the Skim row was not visible in dev:mock and had no e2e test until F-06.6, and F-06.6 skipped it to avoid folding hunks in other tests, which left the Skim row without mock data and its real-app check in the manual field.

Give each mock command the same guard order and error code as its core command: check the fallback refusal before the readiness check, because the F-06.5 mock answered a fallback drag with 'The plan isn't ready yet.' where the core returns INVALID_INPUT, and that mismatch was the only red test. Derive a mock flag from the same source field the core reads (session source kind, headSha), never an id prefix or a design-mock note, and keep per-head flags such as planReady equal across mock rows that share a headSha (F-17.2, F-02.5 review findings).

entries.text: Autopilot roles cannot run /app, so a drag or other pointer behaviour is covered only by the e2e mock; record 'not tried in the real app' in the item's manual field, as F-06.5 did, so the next interactive session runs that check.

When the plan row and the existing code disagree on what a control does, or a status colour or check has combinations nobody defined (reviewed and current, skipped before current), write each reading you chose as a tests-stage decision and make it a red assertion, because F-06.6's Show expanded an inline path list in code while the plan row said it opens the browse, and F-07.1 found two undefined status combinations; both items passed gate 1 without a fix round. Lock an edge state's accessible name, tooltip and shortcut hint the same way (F-30.3: the last step's arrow keeps 'Next step' but opens S-05), since both F-30.3 review nits came from that reading left unlocked. The same holds for an inline editor over an async save: lock the editor-open and save-in-flight combinations (dimmed style lifted, Cancel and Esc during the save, pencil while editing), where all three F-12.3 review nits sat.

Add a test assertion in the same commit for any user-visible copy that the spec and mock do not give, because F-06.6 shipped the '5 of 16 files' summary with a decision note but no test, and review raised it as a nit.

For a fallback test, inject a fetcher that returns an error rather than an empty list, because an empty result never reaches the command's error branch (the review nit on src-tauri/tests/plan_threads.rs line 301).

entries.text: When the tests stage finds an open gap, record it under decisions or a backlog entry rather than notes: F-06.9 left three gaps (threads missing from the plan cache key, counted threads shown in no step, restored steps without thread cards) in notes with decisions empty.

List the e2e locators the implementation must keep (accessible names, role=img text, span order) in the tests verdict notes, as F-07.1 did, and the implementer then passed the full step e2e suite (11/11) with no fix round.
When a new state changes what a design shot shows, seed that state in the shot spec in the same implement commit (F-07.1 marked steps 1 to 3 reviewed for S-03), and the design-check came back clean.

When the pinned Playwright browser is missing on this PC, the tests role reports the e2e command as not run with the missing browser path instead of pointing Playwright at another binary, because F-09.1 claimed an e2e run through a temporary config while the review could not run it and gate-1 verify never runs e2e; the conductor should make the pinned chromium available before the tests stage, since F-09.2 ended with e2e not run (chromium-1248 missing) after 135k tokens against 67k for implement, whose verify then ran the same e2e green.

When a prop changes a component's behaviour (NoteCard selfReview), grep every render site in the tests stage: GuidePanel layout C was left without the prop and the gap went only into tests notes, not decisions or a backlog entry. For shared state that other keys or features read (the J/K current hunk), also grep the milestone plan decisions for its name and lock every existing consumer (C composer start line, Ctrl+Shift+O target) as its own red test, because unlocked M4 decision 13 became the only severe review finding of F-30.6.

For dismiss, undo or any filter keyed by a shared fingerprint, assert what the reload shows for each decision state (open, draft, dismissed), not only the table row: the F-09.4 undo test checked only the dismissals row and passed while a reloaded open note vanished, which only review caught. Pin the restored-after-restart state of a screen the same way, as a red test in the tests stage, because F-17.4 left it to the implementer and review raised the missing progress line after a restart.

entries.text: Give a state-bug fix a regression test that you have seen fail on the old code, as fix-1's resume.rs reload test did (it fails with the old filter), so the green gate proves the fix rather than the table.

Before the tests stage marks a live check as manual, confirm its runner exists (package.json script, tools/ file); when it is missing, plan the runner as its own item, because F-09.5's tests verdict said autopilot could not add the eval:claude harness, the implementer then built it in the same item anyway, and the criterion still ended unticked.

Record the loading and error reading of any copy or button choice that depends on an async query as a tests decision with a red assertion, because the MR fallback during loading (Add to drafts on a self-review) was left in notes and review flagged it; on the implement side, give a screen that chooses its view from a query a loading and error branch instead of the default view, since the self-review session showed the MR stub while the query loaded (F-17.4).

entries.text: Read cached state after a restart through the existing resume hook (useResume, as S-03 does), not the TanStack plan query, because a disabled query never loads the stored plan.

entries.text: When a golden or live test is #[ignore]d, add a non-ignored test in verify that builds its seed and loads it through the production loader with a placeholder executable, because F-09.5's eval seed used a layer name that plan::layer() rejects, so verify stayed green while the live run panicked with PlanNotReady and the item needed a second attempt.

Before committing an assertion, name the production change that would make it fail and drop or turn it into a comment if there is none, because the only review findings in both F-09.5 attempts were assertions that cannot fail (a mock test over static fixture data, and assert!(!cx.fallback) after a loader that always returns false); for a rule that reads a context list (threads, cached notes), empty that list and confirm the tests fail, as F-09.5's empty thread list failed 4 of 6 Rust tests.

entries.text: When an item routes a new source kind to an existing screen, assert content of that screen (the 'Start step 1' button or the plan list) and never the Shell landmark, the router path or page.toHaveURL (the app uses createMemoryRouter, so the URL stays at the origin), because the 'Review plan' landmark and pathname checks passed on an empty StubScreen while review rated the unusable screen severe. When the screen still renders a stub for that source or state, decide its content in the tests stage and lock it, because F-17.1 left it 'outside this item' and the fix round had to build the non-MR plan screen.

entries.text: Put a test that installs a global tracing subscriber or log file in its own tests/*.rs binary (or use the thread-local set_default and match the line by a unique key), and run a new test binary several times before committing, because a 3-test binary sharing the global logger failed 6 of 7 runs in review.

entries.text: When logging a failed Claude step, write only code and message for Claude-originated errors (ClaudeFailed, ClaudeNotSignedIn, ClaudeLimited) and log the detail only for app-written errors, because that detail carries Claude's stderr or result text and NFR-08 keeps Claude output out of logs; cover one Claude code with a canary test.

entries.text: When relaxing an eval's text-matching check to remove a false positive, give the exemption only to the field that caused it (the note body) and add a verify-run unit case for every other field (title, suggested_comment) where the topic and the exempting phrase share one sentence, because F-09.5's first sentence-level fix exempted all three fields and review showed that a title like 'async void, already raised in the open thread' would pass the item's only check, which cost a fix round.

When a locked e2e assertion compares a region's text with toHaveText, check whether the region holds CSS text-transform uppercase buttons (Barlow Condensed) and lock it with { useInnerText: true }, because tests/e2e/detailed.spec.ts:78 compared textContent with a captured innerText, could never pass, and cost a test dispute plus a fix round.

Build an in-screen info header as a div with data-testid, not a <header> element, because a second banner landmark breaks the existing role=banner tests of the screen header (F-08.1); list that test id in the tests notes.

Do not override :focus-visible in a component CSS module (keep the global docs/03 outside ring), and check any var(--yellow) element (ring, badge, mark) on the yellow current-row fill, because --focus equals --yellow and the inset yellow ring on Rail's current row was invisible (review severity normal, WCAG 2.4.7, fix round 1) while the structure-only design-check came back clean.

Run npm run typecheck (not only vitest) on the new test files before the tests commit, because vitest strips types and a helper like screen.getAllByRole(...)[0] is HTMLElement | undefined under noUncheckedIndexedAccess, which cost a test dispute and a test-only fix round (F-08.4 helper next()); destructure the first match and throw when it is missing.

When an e2e guard counts or targets getByRole by name (for example radiogroup 'Layout' with toHaveCount(0)), pass exact: true, because Playwright matches names as case-insensitive substrings and the same screen's other required control ('Diff layout') was counted, so all 6 detailed e2e tests failed at the guard and cost a test dispute plus a fix round.

When a Vitest test needs a diff line past the first screenful (about L41) to render a note, mock offsetHeight per element in jsdom (it has no layout) and put that in the tests notes, so the implementer does not chase an empty line list.

When an item adds single-letter shortcuts (N, A, ]) to a screen that has checkboxes, lock a red test that clicks a checkbox and then presses the key, because the shared isTyping treated every input element as typing, so N, A and ] died after the first tick and only review found it (F-08.7 fix round 1). Lock the other side too when users can assign any bare key: every consumer (global shortcuts, Rider key, layout keys) ignores it while focus is in a text field and still acts for a Ctrl chord, because F-19.7's only severe finding was an assigned letter that could no longer be typed in the S-01 input or a comment composer.

Keep locked userEvent tests that type long text well under the 5000 ms vitest timeout (use paste, fireEvent or an explicit per-test timeout), because two locked AskBox cases timed out once when the test step took 94 s instead of 39-55 s, and the implementer could not change them.

Never key React lists by strings that come from Claude's output (read.file, checklist text) without the index, because the core does not dedupe files_read or checklist and duplicates give React key warnings and rows that tick together.

When a UI re-reads a status on a timer because a background run sends no events, define the poll condition as 'any run of the session is in flight, queued or starting included' (not 'the status shows a step running') and pin it with a test where the first read lands before the run reaches Running, because F-08.8's useAnalysisStatus only polled after a read that already had a running step, and review found that a read arriving before the prefetch leaves the queue ends polling and leaves the footer stale.

A core command the UI calls on a timer must run its store reads and per-step cache validation loop inside with_store/spawn_blocking like the commands around it, because review flagged review_analysis_status calling step::cached_analysis (SQLite plus worktree file checks) for every step on the async command thread once a second.

A red e2e never runs the lines after its first failing assertion, so before the tests commit prove the rest can pass: run a scratch copy without the red assertions, run its setup and return path at baseline or in a throwaway variant without the new control, and run a new row or layout locator helper against throwaway markup shaped like the mock (delete the scratch files afterwards). F-08.9's toHaveURL lines behind a red check cost a test dispute and a fix round, F-19.1's broken mock return path pushed out-of-item work onto the implementer (153k tokens), while F-19.3 did this and passed with no dispute and no fix round.

When a milestone decision reverses an existing test (F-07.2 'the last step has no next' expected disabled), name that test and its new expected value in the tests notes, and list the neighbouring assertions that must stay unchanged (F-08.9 end-card tests), so the implementer edits instead of deleting and the locked-tests gate passes first time. Do the same before changing what a mock returns or requires (a suffix moved into a UI helper, a new precondition such as reviewPlan first): grep the existing tests for the full old string and for calls that skip the precondition, as F-02.5 had to change an F-02.2 mock assertion and an F-10.2 mock test asks without a plan.

Build a shortcut from the same predicate its matching button uses (FileBar's deleted-file disable, DiffPane canOpen) and make a key that opens a card or thread reuse an open one instead of resetting it, because Ctrl+Shift+O started Rider on a deleted file and A threw away a streamed Claude answer, both found only by review.

Make a nonce-based reveal or scroll request one-shot by having the consumer (DiffView) remember the last nonce it handled, because choosing the largest nonce among several request sources re-fired the old N reveal after Esc cleared a newer composer reveal and the view jumped back.

For a key handler with a one-shot pause flag (step-start or step-end pause), lock in the tests stage every key that leaves the flagged state without moving off it (paging a tall change, re-measuring), for example ↑ ↓ ↑ at a first change taller than the screen, because the unlocked sequence left pause 'start' set so the next ↑ skipped a whole step, the only severe review finding of the F-30.6 redo.

When a plan row says every key is read from the one shortcuts table, grep the key literals (event.key, 'n', Ctrl+K, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+Shift+O) across src/app and src/screens in the tests stage and lock each consumer with a remap test that fails against a hard-coded matcher, because the first implementation converted only the new walk keys and review found S-04 N/A and the App and Code chords still hard-coded, which cost the fix round.

Write an e2e that pages through content whose height depends on seeded state (an open focused-note callout, viewport size) as 'press until the target change is current, at most N presses, and each extra press must have scrolled', never as an exact press count, because the F-30.6 walk test expected RetryAsync on the third ↓ while a 313 px callout needed a fourth, which cost a test dispute and a test commit in the fix round.

When the same UI state is asserted in both a Vitest file and an e2e spec (F-19.7: the keys button while a capture waits after a refused key), compare the two assertions before the tests commit, because the e2e expected kbd 'N' where ShortcutsChange.test.tsx expected no kbd, no implementation could pass both, and the implementer had to file a test dispute that cost a fix round.

When a tests decision says a card, icon or mark shows in every layout of a shared diff view (Split and Unified), lock one red test per layout and per line kind (added, context, removed), because the F-11.1 tests ran only in Split (beforeEach set layout 'split'), so review found that a thread on a removed line got no gutter icon in Unified, and that cost a severe finding and a fix round.

For any card or composer rendered as a virtualized DiffView row (thread cards, reply composers), have the tests stage lock that the typed text, open composer, busy flag and last error survive an unmount and remount, and have the implementer keep them in the review store keyed by id with mutation results reported through hook-level callbacks, because F-11.2's reply state in useState was lost on scroll-away, review rated it severe and fix-1 cost 110k tokens. Lock the same for anything written anchored to a diff line (line comment, note) across a mode switch (Ctrl+D) and reopening the step: a saved comment stays visible where it was written, also inside a collapsed fold or mechanical hunk, and opening another composer or Undo on another draft never drops typed text (F-09.7). Hook-level callbacks means mutateAsync().then or a hook-level onSuccess, never a per-call mutate onSuccess, which does not run after the card unmounts (F-08.1 lost its 'added' flag and follow-up question).

When gate verify fails only with a 5000 ms Vitest timeout in a test the item did not touch, measure that test with and without the change (here 1.2-1.4 s either way, about 4x slower beside cargo test), then give its describe block an explicit timeout as Footer.test.tsx does and leave the item code alone, as fix-2 did in one small commit (75k tokens). Before editing anything, rerun those files alone and run verify once more, because F-12.4 failed gate 1 and gate 2 on such untouched tests and passed gate 3 with the same commits and no fix.

Never use git stash or stash pop in a lane worktree, because refs/stash is shared by every worktree of the repo and F-11.3's implementer popped another lane's stash (m3/self-review) with conflicts, stray files and two foreign stashes left behind; park work in a WIP commit, or compare with git diff <base> -- <path>.

When the core decides which file a thread (or any path-keyed record) belongs to by both old and new path (thread_place::same_file), lock a renamed-file case in the tests stage (a record written on the old path of a file renamed later) on S-03 and S-04, and use one shared matcher in the UI and mock, because the UI filtered by new path only and that was F-11.3's only severe review finding (threads vanished on renamed files), fixed in fix-1 with a shared threadOnFile and new regression tests.

Keep every new test file under the ~400-line convention by planning the split in the tests stage (one file per describe group, such as a restored-start block), because the F-12.2 SummaryTabs.test.tsx came out at 424 lines and the only review finding was a nit on its size, while the implementer's own SummaryTabsThreads.test.tsx was already split out. Before appending AC tests to an existing file (Rust *_tests.rs included), check its line count and open a sibling file when it would pass ~400 lines (decisions_tests.rs reached 476, F-08.3 nit).

For a label or message that appears after a click (running, suggested, failed), grep how the sibling screen announces the same kind of state (StepNotes puts 'Claude is reading this step…' in role=status) and lock the same live-region role in a red test, because F-12.4 shipped its running and suggested labels as bare <label>s and review rated that the one normal finding (WCAG 4.1.3), which cost a 66k-token fix round.

Before locking a computed style that the mock gets from a native control (accent-color on a checkbox), check how the shared component renders it and assert what it actually paints (box background or tone class), because the F-12.4 e2e asserted accentColor on the button-role Checkbox, which forced a dead accent-color line and an extra class into the shared component and review flagged it as a nit.

Before the tests stage records a decision about a control's label or enabled state, grep the milestone plan decisions for that label (e.g. 'Publish summary') and lock nothing the plan contradicts, because F-12.5's 'a summary alone is not publishable' went against M5 decision 7 and became a severe review finding, and the unchecked restored-start test it locked (MrSummaryPublish.test.tsx:509) could not be changed without a test dispute. When a decision changes what a key does, grep every control, card, footer and Settings row that shows that key's hint and let the newer decision beat an older mock: a hint on a control names only a key that triggers it (F-07.10 locked a stale Space hint because Main.dc.html drew it).

Close, or lock as a red test, any gap that makes a GitLab write send stale, unticked or duplicate content (retry of an edited or unticked draft, a failed summary swallowed, a sent flag held only in a query cache) in the core pass instead of listing it under GAPS in notes, because impl-core listed them, review rated two as severe, and closing them cost fix-1 215k tokens plus a migration and a new DELETE endpoint.

In a Rust test file make a refused connection with a std::net::TcpListener bound on 127.0.0.1:0 and then dropped (as tests/gitlab_client.rs:170), never a dropped wiremock MockServer (it returns to the pool and keeps answering 404), and run cargo test plus cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings on the file before locking it, because both defects in publish_drafts.rs kept verify red in both implement passes and forced a test dispute.

To prove a negative-property test (nothing but draft notes is sent, never approve) can fail, send the forbidden request from a scratch copy of the test against the wiremock and delete it afterwards, because a temporary approve call inside production draft_notes.rs was blocked by the permission classifier in F-12.6.

When an item adds a new row shape for an existing entity (a drafts-only session with empty SHAs, no mr_json and a NULL repo_id), list in the tests stage every existing command the screen calls on it (drafts_publish, claude_summary_comment, session_mr, folders) and lock each against the real core path with that row. F-12.7 locked only session_mr and folders, the mock-backed Publish test passed without a diff, and drafts_publish failing on the real backend became the severe review finding that cost a whole fix round.

In a test of rows moved between sessions, build the expected rows from the pre-move values with session_id mapped to the new session, and check how an id is minted before locking that it survives the move. F-12.7's line-198 assertion could never pass (a test dispute carried through four stages). Its locked 'step_id stays' rule gave a wrong S-04 rail count, because step ids are minted per plan as s1..sN. The mock also could not be aligned without a second dispute.

Before recording an implement-stage decision that reverses a decision in tests.json, grep the locked tests for that behaviour and run them. F-12.7 pass 1 made the Review tile skip drafts-only sessions against a locked e2e and the tests-stage decision, did not run e2e, edited its own Dock test to match, and pass 2 had to revert all of it.
